source.title: On Reasoning Strength Planning in Large Reasoning Models
source.authors: Leheng Sheng; An Zhang; Zijian Wu; Weixiang Zhao; Changshuo Shen; Yi Zhang; Xiang Wang; Tat-Seng Chua

record.tranche_reason: The study uses probing, activation-direction analysis, and activation steering to test whether pre-generation question activations encode and causally affect subsequent reasoning length. This is a conceptual test of pre-caching, not a test of predicting particular future token identities.
record.gate_note: The study reports that reasoning length is predictable from pre-generation activations and that steering those activations changes reasoning length. Its overthink examples are deliberately induced and are not evidence about spontaneous overthinking. Performance results and the end-of-reasoning-logit analyses do not directly measure the versions here; the naïve logit-scaling experiments are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study finds that a property of the future generation, reasoning length, is linearly readable from the <think>-position state before any reasoning token is generated. Steering along a pre-allocated direction changes that length. This is internal look-ahead in multi-step math reasoning, a new setting for V5. It does not test future-token identities (V2), rhyme (V1, V4), or whether the features exist because they help later positions rather than as a side effect (V3).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that LRMs pre-plan reasoning length before generation: it is linearly predictable from question activations and encoded by a pre-allocated direction whose magnitude causally sets reasoning-token count. They add that the direction acts mainly by lowering or raising the </think> logit, and they propose overthink detection and efficient-inference uses.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear regression probes, difference-in-means activation directions, and activation steering to investigate reasoning length, rather than future-token anticipation or rhyme interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction improves with layer depth. The Llama-8B model is described as more sensitive to steering strength; its steering sweep is reported separately in Table 10.

fits_no_version.finding: Difficulty-contrast vectors at the <think> position share one direction (cosine ~0.99), and their norm grows with difficulty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning models encode question difficulty along a single pre-generation direction whose magnitude tracks expected reasoning budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering mainly shifts the </think> logit, much more than random or EOS tokens. Naively scaling that logit (Table 3) is unstable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A pre-planned length signal acts through end-of-reasoning token logits.

record.problems: Probe results are presented largely as plots, with few individual values stated in the text. The study focuses mainly on Qwen-family reasoning models, and the authors note that other model backbones remain underexplored. The evidence concerns reasoning-token quantity rather than specific future-token identities.
record.rows_left_out: Not included: Figure 10’s easy-task steering results because the text does not identify model-specific values; Appendix D’s overthink-detection comparison because overthink questions are deliberately induced; accuracy results are not direct measurements of pre-caching. The end-of-reasoning-token logit analyses and naïve logit-scaling results are not rows for the listed versions.

untested.parts: No rhyme or verse; no frontier model.
Predicts a scalar length, not identities of tokens several positions ahead.
Does not test whether <think>-position features are computed because they help later positions rather than as a byproduct, e.g. of encoding question difficulty.
No rhyme planning, although the models are open-weight.
No test of how far ahead the plan reaches. No comparison against local features or heuristics such as a difficulty-only predictor.

missing.what: Steering effect on reasoning tokens for five models on GPQA diamond and LiveCodeBench, including non-monotonic/reversed responses for R1-Distill-Qwen-14B under positive λ
Steering on easy tasks (MMLU, MATH500 Level 1) reduces tokens without accuracy loss
The probe predicts longer lengths for overthink-attack prompts than for vanilla AlpacaEval prompts. The prompts are induced, but this shows the probe transfers out of domain.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked everything to V3. V3's distinguishing claim (features computed for later positions, not as a side effect) is not tested, so the probe and steering rows are relinked to V5 (look-ahead in multi-step reasoning). Caveats: the direction comes from difficulty contrasts and the probes have no difficulty-only baseline, so the 'plan' may be a difficulty encoding. Steering is applied at all layers and positions, so causal evidence is not specific to the pre-generation state. The evidence concerns a scalar length, not future content.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test rhyme-word representations or whether intervening on candidate rhyme words changes verse.
The study predicts reasoning-token counts, not the identity of tokens several positions ahead.

It tests pre-generation features that causally affect reasoning length, but not whether those features are computed specifically for later positions rather than also being a byproduct of next-token prediction; it does not test specific future-token content.
The models are open-weight, but the study does not test rhyme planning or use open attribution-graph or probing tools for rhyme.
The study does not test multi-step reasoning plans, chess, or Sokoban as future-token look-ahead tasks.
The study does not argue that look-ahead is shallow or incidental, or that local next-token features explain future-token planning.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B
rows.operation_detail: Steer activations with the pre-allocation vector.
rows.value: MATH500: 3457.01 at λ=0; AIME2024: 11049.53 at λ=0; OlympiadBench: 7234.64 at λ=0; token counts vary across the reported λ values
rows.note: The table reports all λ-specific counts; the text says the model is more sensitive to steering strength. Effects are not monotonic across the full λ sweep.
rows.check: Relink to V5. The λ range is ten times smaller (±0.02). The overall direction holds (MATH500: 3042 at −0.02 to 3654 at +0.02), but it is non-monotonic within the sweep, e.g. AIME 11049 at 0 vs 10775 at +0.005.

source_check.correct: State: observed for V5. Length changes under steering, with non-monotonic responses within the sweep; V5 does not require monotonic length control.
source_check.problem: Non-monotonic steering alone does not establish incomplete look-ahead under V5.

relationships.condition: Qwen-family LRMs (R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B–32B, QwQ-32B) on MATH and related math sets
relationships.reason: Pre-generation probes reach r>0.8 for reasoning length, and steering along the pre-allocation direction moves length monotonically with λ (R1–R6, R18–R22).
relationships.display_finding: Pre-generation probes predicted reasoning length with correlations above 0.8, and steering along the pre-allocation direction changed length monotonically with steering strength.

relationships.condition: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B; and R1-Distill-Qwen-14B on GPQA/LiveCodeBench code generation (from text, Tables 4, 6)
relationships.reason: Llama-8B needs a tenfold smaller λ and responds non-monotonically (R23). Per the text, 14B tokens fall under positive steering on GPQA (6366→5137) and code generation, so the steering effect depends on model and task.
relationships.display_finding: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B required tenfold weaker steering and responded non-monotonically; positive steering reduced R1-Distill-Qwen-14B's token total from 6366 to 5137 on GPQA and also shortened code generation.

tranche.reason: Tests internal anticipation of reasoning length in mathematical reasoning, a new setting beyond verse.

source_check.notes: Steering occurs at every layer and position, so it does not isolate a causal effect of the pre-generation state alone. No difficulty-only or question-length probe baseline is reported; the authors' conclusion paraphrase is faithful, but stronger than that isolated causal claim warrants.

statements.problem: The tenfold smaller tested λ range is correct, but necessity is not demonstrated by a comparison with the larger range.

statements.correction: Llama-8B: tested λ range ±0.02, versus ±0.2 for Qwen models; greater steering sensitivity stated; non-monotonic token counts in Table 10.
